mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a financial crisis with inverted yield curve.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which pressures firms to raise wages and prices, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or during periods of unusually high productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals weakening household demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or during periods of offsetting fiscal stimulus.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or during periods of strong export demand.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual monetary tightening and inflationary pressure, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or during periods of collapsing commodity prices.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 6-month moving average, combined with a stable unemployment rate, indicates robust labor market expansion that boosts consumer spending and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 6-month moving average AND UNRATE unchanged ±0.1pp
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or during periods of wage-price spirals.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or during periods of rising mortgage rates.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (RSAFS) and Industrial Production (INDPRO) for two consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of monetary policy stance.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and INDPRO both decline for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or during periods of strong fiscal stimulus offsetting the decline.
